transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… um, I guess I came in because I feel like I can’t keep things organized at all right now. Like, I’m trying to handle my schoolwork and also this little accessories shop I’ve been doing, and everything just turns into piles—supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes.

And then I’ll be like, “Okay, I’m going to sort this,” but then I find a receipt from two weeks ago or a note for an assignment, and I don’t know what I’m supposed to do first. It sounds kind of small when I say it, but it’s been really overwhelming.
Have you had trouble staying organized and keeping track of tasks since you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. My mom actually kept some of my elementary school notes, which is kind of embarrassing—she saves everything, like old birthday cards and random permission slips too—but some of the notes from teachers said I was always getting out of my seat or talking before I was called on.

And there were things about me rushing through group activities, even when I understood the work. I don’t know if that’s exactly “organized,” but it was like I couldn’t slow down or stay on the process the way everyone else was.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks once you’ve started them?

Yeah, I do. I’ll start something and think I’m doing it, but if there are like three or four steps, I usually do the first part and then somehow miss the rest.

Like if a teacher gives instructions, or even with vendor stuff for my little shop, I’ll leave the meeting thinking, “Okay, got it,” and then later I realize I didn’t attach the form or I didn’t finish the last part of an order note. And then I’m scrambling to fix it. It’s frustrating because it’s not that I don’t care—I just… miss pieces.
Do these problems with staying organized and finishing things happen in more than one part of your life, like both school and work?

Yeah, definitely more than one place. It’s like school and the accessories shop kind of collide in my head. I’ll have assignment notes and due dates mixed in with receipts and supply stuff, and then I make piles because I’m like, “Okay, I’ll sort it later,” but later the piles are just… bigger.

And then I don’t know whether I’m supposed to start with the class thing or the shop thing, or like, find the receipt first—oh, I actually bought these little bead containers thinking they’d fix everything, which is funny because now some of them are just sitting in a bag. But yeah, it’s both. I can’t really keep either one organized when they’re happening at the same time.
Do you find yourself repeatedly arranging, checking, or redoing things because it feels like they have to be just right?

Um… I don’t think so? Like, I check things sometimes, but not in a “it has to be perfect” way, I guess. More like I’m trying to remember if I even did it.

The “just right” thing—like arranging stuff over and over—doesn’t really sound like me. I mean, I’ll move things around on my desk and then find a receipt from two weeks ago and suddenly start thinking about whether I ordered more clasps, but that’s not really… redoing it because it feels wrong. It’s more like I got distracted. So, yeah, I’m not sure that’s a big thing for me.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

I don’t know if I’d call it worrying a lot. I mean, I worry when there’s something actually happening, like if I forgot to do something or I have to get something turned in, but just sitting there worrying about a bunch of different stuff for no reason… I’m not sure.

Sometimes my head feels busy, but that’s different than worry, I think. Like I’ll be thinking about one thing and then remember something else, and then I’m like, wait, why did I come in here? But I don’t know if that’s what you mean. So… maybe not really?
Have these problems caused you to do worse in school or with your shop than you know you’re capable of?

Yeah… I mean, I hate saying that, but yes. I know I can do better than what it looks like on paper right now.

With school, I missed some required steps for my program—like the kind of things you’re supposed to just get done so everything stays moving—and now my financial aid is kind of at risk. Which is really scary, because it’s not like I didn’t care. I just… didn’t keep up with the pieces the way I needed to.

And with the shop stuff, people I’ve worked with on projects have started relying on me less. Like they’ll take over parts or not ask me to handle certain things because I haven’t been consistent. That feels embarrassing, because I know I’m capable of doing good work when I actually get it together.
Before age 12, were you already having these kinds of problems with attention or organization?

Yeah, I think so. My mom actually still has some of my elementary school notes—like from teachers—and they said stuff about me always being out of my seat, talking before I got called on, that kind of thing.

And I remember group activities being kind of… I’d rush through them even if I knew the work, because I just wanted to get to the next part or, I don’t know, not sit there forever. My mom brings those notes up sometimes when she’s cleaning out bins, which she does in this very random way where suddenly there’s a stack of old school papers on the kitchen table. But yeah, it was definitely already showing up back then.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

Um… I don’t think so? Like, I have bad days where I’m frustrated or I feel kind of gross about myself, especially when things pile up, but “depressed most days” sounds… I don’t know, heavier than what I’d say.

Sometimes I’ll wake up already annoyed because there’s stuff I meant to do, and then I’ll end up scrolling for way too long, and then it’s like noon and I’m mad at myself—sorry, that’s kind of not what you asked. But no, I haven’t noticed feeling really down most days lately.
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Yeah, I think it got more obvious after I changed schools. Not like one dramatic thing happened, exactly, but that change… I had to manage the business program stuff and also keep up with my accessories shop with way less structure than before.

It’s been a real problem for, I guess, a little over two years now—like about two years and a couple months. Which is weird to say out loud because time feels kind of fake sometimes, like I’ll think something was last semester and it was actually forever ago. But yeah, since that school change and having to juggle all of that on my own more, it got noticeably harder.
Before you changed schools, were these same problems already causing trouble for you?

Before I changed schools… yeah, I mean, there were issues, but it’s kind of hard to separate because the school change made everything way more obvious.

Like, now it’s actually caused real problems. I missed required steps for my program—stuff I was supposed to handle—and now my financial aid might be at risk, which is… really stressful. And with my accessories shop projects, people have started relying on me less because I’ll miss things or not follow through the way they expected.

Before that, I think people maybe covered for me more, or there was more structure. So it was there, but it didn’t hit consequences this big until after.
When the school change happened, did your attention and organization problems start only after that change?

No, I don’t think it started only after that. It got harder after the school change, but my mom actually still has notes from when I was in elementary school saying I was always getting out of my seat, talking before I was called on, rushing through group activities… even when I understood the work.

Which is kind of embarrassing, honestly, because she kept all those papers in this folder with old report cards and stuff, and I remember being like, “Why do you still have this?” But yeah, it was definitely there way before I changed schools.
